clue.text: British sailor bitten by shaggy monkey-like beast

indicators.note: something bitten is held between the jaws, so the sailor sits inside the shaggy word

parts.note: shaggy hair is bushy
standard abbreviation for British
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A British sailor gets a nasty bite from some hairy ape-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby, or galago, is a small African primate with huge eyes, a monkey relative in the broad sense.

clue.text: Live round centre of Bicester, or near by

indicators.note: the verb for living goes round the outside of the selected letters

parts.note: to bide is to dwell or live

indicators.note: only the two middle letters of the eight-letter town name are kept

parts.note: the fourth and fifth of its eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone lives in or near the Oxfordshire market town of Bicester.
explanation.walkthrough: Bicester is a town in Oxfordshire; its centre is the middle pair of letters, which go inside BIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside is a preposition meaning next to, alongside or close at hand, the same as near by.

clue.text: More disreputable disorder is heard

indicators.note: putting the two words into disorder scrambles their letters

parts.note: the anagram fodder, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A rowdy disturbance is overheard somewhere rather seedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is heard' looks like a sound signal; it is only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady dealings are dubious and dishonest, so the comparative shadier means of worse repute.

clue.text: Country music on the lawn?

parts.note: the real reading: a style of American folk music from Kentucky
the playful reading: a kind of turf grass growing on a lawn

explanation.walkthrough: Kentucky is nicknamed after a meadow grass, and its fiddle-and-banjo music took the same name, so the question mark invites the garden reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is both a genre of country music and a meadow grass of the genus Poa, used for lawns.

clue.text: Rough estimate of cost of statue at baseball venue

definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: a sculpted figure standing in a stadium

explanation.surface: Someone prices a statue to be put up at a baseball stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: A figure can be a sculpture, and a ballpark is an American baseball ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is the idiom for an approximate number, close enough to be in the right range.

clue.text: Some tweeds Pa desired for a suit

indicators.note: only part of the following run of letters is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Father fancied some tweed cloth to have a suit made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like tailoring to match the tweeds, but it is a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Good temper that envelops city

indicators.note: the phrase wraps around the wanted name, holding it inside

parts.note: the letters straddle the gap between the last two words

explanation.surface: A city whose residents are blessed with an even, good-natured temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good' only dresses the surface; the city sits across 'temper that'. Perth is a Scottish city as well as the Australian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Perth is a city both in central Scotland on the Tay and in Western Australia.

clue.text: Part company with daughter — one on Fringe

parts.note: standard abbreviation for daughter
the Roman numeral for one
a verge is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A daughter performing at the Edinburgh Fringe leaves her family behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just puts the one before the edge. The Fringe is the Edinburgh arts festival, which the capital letter suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths that diverge separate and go different ways, which is what parting company means.

clue.text: Peace is unknown after wandering in trees

indicators.note: letters that wander stray from their starting order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: Peace is something you will never find after getting lost in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the unknown behind the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenity is calm tranquillity, a state of inner peace.

clue.text: From which to pay electricity charges

definitions.text: From which to pay electricity charges

parts.note: the real reading: a bank account used for everyday payments
the playful reading: a bill for the electric power used

explanation.walkthrough: Electricity is current, so the clue doubles as a description of the power bill itself and of where you pay it from.
explanation.definitionFit: A current account is the British name for a checking account, the everyday bank account bills are paid from.

clue.text: Marine creature capturing heart of regular flier

indicators.note: the marine creature takes the extracted letters captive inside itself

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal

indicators.note: only the central letters of the following word are used

parts.note: the middle three of its seven letters

explanation.surface: A sea creature traps the centre of a frequent traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular flier' reads as a frequent passenger, but 'regular' is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagull is a bird, and anything that flies can be called a flier.

clue.text: Don, say, on horseback first away from coast

parts.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up
the Don is a river, in Russia and in Yorkshire and Aberdeenshire

explanation.surface: A university don goes riding inland from the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like an academic but is a river. 'First' only places the riding term in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upriver means travelling towards the source, inland and away from the sea.

clue.text: Performing pet, popular inside

indicators.note: the second element sits within the first

parts.note: a dog is a common pet
something in is in fashion, popular

explanation.surface: A performing pet animal goes down well with an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a task is carrying it out, the present participle matching performing.

clue.text: Former Argentine leader caught costly French horse

indicators.note: the leader's name catches and holds the other word inside it

parts.note: Juan Perón, president of Argentina
cher is French for expensive

explanation.surface: A former Argentine president is snared by an expensive French racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' belongs with 'costly', asking for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Percheron is a heavy draught horse breed from the Perche region of France.

clue.text: E German partner overturned deal agreed in advance

indicators.note: turning things over upsets their order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: An East German partner tore up a deal that had already been agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E German' reads as East German, but the E is just one more letter of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A prearrangement is something settled or fixed beforehand, an advance agreement.

clue.text: Oriental, maybe, set out in profitable venture

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the venture
out signals the short word is rearranged, put out of order

parts.note: the short word, letters rearranged
a money-maker is an earner

explanation.surface: Someone from the Far East sets up a money-making business.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oriental is a person from the East, one example of an easterner, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: One who twists round foot of rival fighter

indicators.note: the twisting person goes around the outside of the selected letter

parts.note: to wrest is to twist or wrench, so one doing it is a wrester

indicators.note: the foot of a word in a down clue is its last letter

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A fighter grabs an opponent by the foot and twists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who twists' feels like the definition, since wrestlers twist limbs; it is the outer wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler is a combat sportsman who grapples with an opponent, a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Things due, | hear, to lobby for life's milestones

indicators.note: what the setter hears is a word said rather than spelt

parts.note: entitlements are rights
belonging to a lobby is being of a passage, a lobby being a passageway

explanation.surface: Campaigners press their claims in a lobby on behalf of life's big moments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase sounds like rights of passage, things owed to a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites of passage are the ceremonies marking key life stages such as birth, coming of age, marriage and death.

clue.text: Half of this sketch is done

indicators.note: only the first two of the four letters are kept

parts.note: its first half
a rough is a preliminary sketch

explanation.surface: An artist has finished half of a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be through is to be finished, so it matches done in the sense of completed.

clue.text: Dance entry pulling in most of ballot

indicators.note: the entry draws the shortened word inside it

parts.note: a gate is a way in

indicators.note: all but the final letter is kept

parts.note: a ballot is a vote

explanation.surface: A dance contest entry pulls in the bulk of the votes cast.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French dance in moderate four-four time, popular in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Occult elements of oath I'd denied

indicators.note: the answer is made of component parts drawn from the run of words

parts.note: spans the three words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Elements of the occult in a sworn oath that someone denied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occult' suggests the supernatural, but its root sense is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult originally means concealed or secret, so it is a synonym of hidden.

clue.text: Tiger cats trained to be of value militarily

indicators.note: animals that are trained are reshaped into new behaviour

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Big cats are trained up for use in war.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strategic is important to the overall plan of a war, such as a strategic bridge or port.

clue.text: Possibly spring seasons

definitions.meaning: first meaning: spring ... are one kind of the sea's rise and fall
second meaning: an old word for times of year, as in Yuletide

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' and 'seasons' look like one idea, but spring here is a kind of tide.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide is the periodic rise and fall of the sea, and in archaic use a season or festival time.

clue.text: Closing words in song for siren voices

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: The final lines of a song are written to be sung by sirens.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the concealment; 'voices' simply houses the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a ballad or poem, addressed to a patron or reader.

clue.text: Wash slab ignoring edges and below

indicators.note: the first and last letters are disregarded, keeping the inside

parts.note: its two inner letters
a direct synonym

explanation.surface: Someone scrubs a stone slab, missing the edges and the underside.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash and iron clothes, so it matches the verb wash.

clue.text: Nude dancing outside, not without being observed

indicators.note: a dancing body moves about, as these letters do
the rearranged letters go around the next word

parts.note: the letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dances naked out of doors and nobody spots them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase standing for the adjective: something done unnoted is done without being observed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnoted means unremarked or unnoticed, describing something that happened without being seen.

clue.text: New design for old material has her worried

indicators.note: something worried is fretted at and pulled about, disturbing its arrangement

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A dressmaker frets over restyling some old fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old ideas or content reworked and presented as fresh, a recycling of material.

clue.text: Fish — first of trout caught by sawbones

indicators.note: the doctor catches the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: sawbones is slang for a surgeon

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its initial letter

explanation.surface: A surgeon lands a trout on a fishing trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large primitive fish, famous as the source of caviar.
